dedupe_keys.name: carbon neutral pathways for the united states case

description: Williams and colleagues studied how the United States could reach net-zero or net-negative energy and industrial carbon dioxide emissions by 2050. Evolved Energy Research publishes detailed model outputs and an input-summary workbook for this national case at the linked GitHub repository. The study connects EnergyPATHWAYS demand scenarios for 16 U.S. regions to RIO supply optimisation, with infrastructure decisions at five-year intervals and sampled hourly operations. It tests eight decarbonisation scenarios against a reference case. The article reports a 2050 net cost of 0.2–1.2% of GDP across its pathways and identifies renewable build-out, coal retirement and electrification as shared near-term actions. Those figures are modelled findings, not observed outcomes. The workbooks use XLSX format and the repository states MIT terms with free access. Its main limit for reuse is that the repository contains result and input-summary workbooks, but it does not publish a complete self-contained RIO execution package there. This case can provide scenario benchmarks and technology assumptions for electricity, gas, transport and building capacity-planning studies. The catalogue's MESSAGEix framework is another energy modelling method; it was not used in this case. No workbook was downloaded and no scenario was reproduced.
